interface.title: CDFuse — NetCDF comparison (CDFuse v1.0.0)
interface.field: Earth and environmental science: hydrology, climate and remote-sensing evaluation of gridded data
interface.stage_of_work: Validating and benchmarking model, reanalysis or satellite outputs against observations
interface.what_it_is_for: Line up a candidate gridded NetCDF dataset with a reference dataset in time and space, compute per-cell skill metrics (NSE, KGE, PBIAS, RMSE, MAE, Bias, Correlation), show them as maps with summary statistics, and export reproducible outputs.

data.note: I used the built-in demonstration pair (demo_candidate.nc and demo_reference.nc), loaded with 'Load demonstration data' on the 1 · Data tab. It is a synthetic 1° grid of 27 lat × 29 lon over 180 days. The candidate is the reference with +12% scaling, a +0.15 offset, noise and a block of missing data. No files were uploaded because there were no test files. 127.0.0.1 showed a blank page; http://localhost:8501 worked.

tree.general: Judge how well one gridded dataset reproduces a reference dataset, cell by cell, and keep the evidence
tree.specific: Compare a candidate NetCDF against a reference NetCDF in CDFuse and export the metric maps, tables and run report

features.name: Paired coordinate mapper with extra-dimension slicer
features.general: For each of two datasets, auto-guess which fields are time, latitude and longitude, let the user override each guess, and ask which slice to use for any dimension left over
features.specific: Candidate and Reference columns, each with Variable, Time, Latitude and Longitude coordinate dropdowns plus variable long-name, units and dimension sizes. Leaving a dimension unassigned reveals 'Additional dimensions — choose the slice to compare'
steps: Read the auto-detected variable, units and dimension sizes
Open a coordinate dropdown and pick another field
If a dimension is left unassigned, pick its slice value from the selector that appears
Restore the correct mapping and the slice selector disappears
serves_tasks: Confirm or correct which fields hold time, latitude and longitude in each dataset

features.name: Per-dataset time alignment: shift plus one-hour-per-day filter
features.general: Line up the time axes of two series by shifting one by a set number of hours and, optionally, keeping one chosen hour per day from each and pairing them by calendar date
features.specific: Time shift (hours) number inputs for each dataset; Sub-daily sampling radio (Use every timestamp / Keep one hour per day) with independent Candidate hour (UTC) and Reference hour (UTC) selectors and a Match on calendar date checkbox. The effect is listed in the 'What CDFuse did to your data' notes
steps: Enter a time shift in hours for either dataset
Choose Keep one hour per day
Pick the hour to keep for candidate and for reference
Leave Match on calendar date ticked to pair different hours by date
Read the processing notes after running to confirm what was kept and shifted
serves_tasks: Shift one dataset's clock so its timestamps line up with the other's
Keep only one sampling time per day from each dataset and pair them by date
Check what processing was applied and how many time steps and cells were matched

features.name: Temporal aggregation and grid-alignment selector
features.general: Choose a period to summarise to, a statistic for summarising, and which of two grids becomes the common grid (or keep only shared cells), then see how many time steps and cells survive
features.specific: Temporal aggregation (None/Daily/Monthly/Seasonal DJF-MAM-JJA-SON/Annual), Aggregation statistic (Mean/Sum/Minimum/Maximum/Median) and Spatial alignment (Interpolate candidate to reference grid / Interpolate reference to candidate grid / Use exact shared coordinates only, linear interpolation). The Overview shows matched time steps and lat/lon cells
steps: Pick the temporal aggregation period
Pick the aggregation statistic
Pick the spatial alignment method
Run and read matched time steps (180 / 6 / 3) and the alignment note in the processing list
serves_tasks: Choose the time period to summarise over
Choose the statistic used to summarise each period
Decide how the two grids are brought onto common cells
Check what processing was applied and how many time steps and cells were matched

features.name: Metric picker with inline definitions
features.general: Choose a set of agreement scores from a chip list, with a 'select all' option and an expandable glossary of what each score means and its ideal value
features.specific: 'Metrics to calculate' multiselect (Correlation, NSE, KGE, PBIAS, RMSE, MAE, Bias) with Select all, removable chips and Clear all, plus the 'What these metrics mean' expander. The chosen set decides which maps and table rows appear
steps: Open the list and press Select all or add single metrics
Remove unwanted metrics with each chip's ×
Open 'What these metrics mean' to read ranges and ideal values
Run and see only the chosen metrics in the table and maps
serves_tasks: Pick which agreement scores to compute
Read the overall score statistics and coverage to judge agreement

features.name: Summary statistics table with coverage
features.general: One row per score with mean, median, min, max, number of valid cells and percent of the grid scored, so overall agreement and how much of the area it rests on can be read together
features.specific: Summary statistics table on 3 · Results with Mean/Median/Min/Max/Valid cells/Coverage % per metric; the standard table toolbar allows sorting, searching and hiding columns
steps: Read each metric's mean, median, min and max
Read Valid cells and Coverage % to see how much of the grid was scored
Optionally sort by a column or search for a metric row to find it quickly
serves_tasks: Read the overall score statistics and coverage to judge agreement

features.name: Per-metric score map with stats panel and multi-format export
features.general: For each score, show a colour map of its value per grid cell (missing cells blank), fixed colour scales suited to the score, the score's summary numbers beside it, and buttons to export that one map as image, gridded file, georeferenced raster or table
features.specific: Maps section: one matplotlib lat/lon map per metric (e.g. diverging -1..1 for Correlation, -100..100% for PBIAS) with Mean/Median/Minimum/Maximum and PNG / NetCDF / GeoTIFF / CSV download buttons. PNG, NetCDF and GeoTIFF downloads were confirmed; the CSV button is unreliable: pbias.csv came down with lat, lon, value rows and empty masked cells, but Correlation's CSV arrived under a random hex name and could not be read
steps: Scroll to a metric's map
Read the description line and colour bar
Spot blank cells where data were missing
Compare with the Mean/Median/Min/Max panel
Download the map as PNG, NetCDF or GeoTIFF (check any CSV download opens)
serves_tasks: Look at where on the map agreement is good or poor for each score
Download each score map as an image, a gridded data file, a georeferenced raster and a table

features.name: Processing provenance log, run report and output bundle
features.general: After a run, list in plain words every transformation applied to the data (filters, shifts, aggregation, matched steps, regridding), and save the same list with all settings as a text report alongside the summary table and an archive of all outputs
features.specific: 'What CDFuse did to your data' expander on 3 · Results; Run report (.txt) with a SETTINGS block, PROCESSING NOTES and a note on how missing values are handled; Summary CSV and All outputs (.zip) buttons below the summary table
steps: Run a comparison
Open 'What CDFuse did to your data'
Check the shift, hour filter, aggregation and alignment notes
Download Run report (.txt) for the record
Download Summary CSV and All outputs (.zip) to keep the full result set
serves_tasks: Check what processing was applied and how many time steps and cells were matched
Download the summary table, a written record of settings, and an archive of everything

features.name: Built-in known-answer demonstration pair
features.general: A synthetic candidate/reference pair with a documented, known distortion (scaling, offset, noise and a block of missing data) that can be loaded in one click to check that the scores come out as expected
features.specific: 'No data to hand? Load the built-in demonstration pair' expander on 1 · Data with Load demonstration data and Download demo candidate/reference (.nc) buttons; the candidate is the reference with +12% scaling, +0.15 offset, noise and a missing block on a 27×29, 180-day grid
steps: Open the 'No data to hand?' expander
Read the description of the built-in distortion
Press Load demonstration data; both files appear in the sidebar
Run a comparison and check the scores reflect the known bias and missing block

features.name: Workflow checklist and session reset
features.general: A side panel that ticks off the stages of the comparison as they are completed and a button that clears all loaded data and results to start again
features.specific: Sidebar workflow checklist (load, configure, run, results) and Session panel with Clear session, after which it shows 'Nothing loaded yet'. The 'Run comparison' tick can lag until the next rerun
steps: Watch checklist items turn green as data are loaded and a run finishes
Press Clear session
Confirm the checklist resets and 'Nothing loaded yet' shows
